newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN WOOL INDICATOR RISES 3 CENTS TO 703C/KG.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN WOOL INDICATOR RISES 3 CENTS TO 703C/KG.

text.p: The Australian wool market eastern indicator rose three cents to 703 cents a kg clean on Thursday at sales in Sydney and Adelaide, Wool International said.
Merino fleece was mostly dearer, with 19/26 microns 0.5 percent dearer, 20/23m slightly dearer, 21/22m one percent dearer and 24/25m up to 0.5 per cent cheaper.
Merino skirtings were firm, while in crossbreds, 27m was slightly cheaper and 28-31m unchanged.
In cardings, locks were one percent cheaper and crutchings generally unchanged.
WI said Japanese interests and China were principal buyers with good support from most sectors of the trade.
Of the 23,642 bales offered, 5.7 percent were passed in.
In early Fremantle trading, merino fleece of 20/24/25m was unchanged, 21m fully firm, 22m generally unchanged, and 23m one percent dearer while merino skirtings were generally unchanged.
Sales continue next week in Sydney and Melbourne with about 79,450 bales to be offered.
